rationale: One shared alpha (5000) applies the same shrinkage to all 200 drugs, but per-drug signal varies a lot. A few drugs, mostly targeted oncology drugs, have strong expression biomarkers, while many non-oncology drugs are close to noise. Picking a ridge alpha separately for each drug with efficient leave-one-out on the training fold (RidgeCV GCV, `alpha_per_target=True`) should loosen shrinkage on the strong-signal drugs and shrink more on the noisy ones, at almost no extra compute cost.

Lineage drives a lot of drug sensitivity. A shared ridge with α=5000 on 5,000 standardized genes shrinks it down to a weak expression proxy. This change adds one-hot OncotreeLineage indicators, scaled ×20 so they carry an effective penalty of only about 12.5 instead of 5000. Each drug then gets its own lightly shrunk per-lineage offset, while expression explains what is left within each lineage.

A single shared ridge penalty (alpha=5000) is too much shrinkage for drugs with strong expression signal (e.g. targeted MEK/BRAF/EGFR inhibitors) and too little for noisy non-oncology drugs. This change picks each drug's alpha separately with efficient leave-one-line-out CV (RidgeCV in GCV mode, alpha_per_target) on the training fold only. Each cell line is its own group, so leave-one-out matches grouped CV. If any group has more than one line, the code falls back to grouped 5-fold CV.

Use one ridge penalty per drug, picked by efficient leave-one-out (GCV) inside the training fold, instead of a single alpha=5000 for all drugs. Changing the penalty changes the direction of the fitted weights, so it changes each drug's Pearson r. With about 380 lines and 5,000 genes, the kernel form makes this almost free.

A lot of PRISM drug sensitivity follows tissue of origin, but with alpha=5000 spread over 5,000 genes, the ridge model shrinks away most of that lineage signal. This change adds one-hot OncotreeLineage indicators to the gene features, merging lineages with fewer than 5 training lines into "other". The indicators are scaled up by 10 so ridge penalises them about 100× less than the genes. Each drug then gets a per-lineage offset, and expression explains what is left.
